_comment: Golden corpus for the rule packs. Run with: python tests/run_corpus.py
expect  - these rule ids MUST produce at least one hit on this file.
reject  - these rule ids MUST produce ZERO hits on this file.
The 'reject' cases are the ones that matter. Detection regressions are loud; precision
regressions are silent, and a rule that flags parameterized SQL teaches engineers to
ignore the whole report. Every new rule should arrive with at least one reject case
drawn from its own falsePositiveHints field.
Note: this exercises the rule pass only - the deterministic sensor. It cannot test the
triage layer, which is where reachability and severity are actually decided.

cases.label: dotnet: parameterized SQL is NOT injection
dotnet: MarkupString is an XSS sink
dotnet: plain interpolation is auto-encoded, not a sink
dotnet: [Authorize] present satisfies the absence check
python: %s parameter binding is NOT injection
python: pickle.loads / yaml.load are unsafe deserialization
javascript: innerHTML assignment is an XSS sink
javascript: textContent is not a sink
universal: a real-looking credential is a secret
universal: templated and empty values are NOT secrets
universal: wordy placeholders DO fire (sensor cannot judge; triage drops them)
cases.note: Documents the division of labour honestly. A regex cannot separate 'your-api-key-here' from a real credential without a wordlist, and a wordlist would be incomplete while creating false confidence. The sensor fires; triage is responsible for dropping it.
